answer: An agent marketplace can weight votes by tokens locked for 30 days, rather than by account count. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand agents still buys only 100 tokens of influence, so a plume of new identities cannot amplify the attacker's signal. To gain more control, the attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, paying capital costs and bearing price risk. Disposable accounts offer no cheap harbor for extra voting power.
